resolved_findings.resolution: RCoA 2026 pp2–3 and p6 plus GOSH Important things to tell us directly corroborate anesthetic medication/allergy/history and last food/drink disclosure. RCH and FDA separately support child product/weight checks and overdose/duplicate-product liver risk. Elective fasting hours and cardiac-specific instructions are excluded.

Mayo When to see a doctor and Nemours What Should I Do/Get Help Right Away separately describe spontaneous untwisting and prompt care after relief. AUA p5 supplies intermittent history with normal examination/ultrasound and possible elective fixation after current assessment; it is not substituted with manual-detorsion evidence.

APSA pediatric torsion aftercare and CUH4011v11 pediatric postoperative no-fluid contact corroborate the child hydration action. RCH supports persistent vomiting; MercyOne/Whittington general postoperative advice covers the broader context without their timing being exported. CUH102551 and COGv6 separately support mechanical protection of the remaining testis; only shared anatomy/impact protection transfers, with no cancer fertility rules or quantified torsion-prevention effect.

EAU8.3.3 now bound for delayed assessment, EAU8.2 plus AUA p5 for intermittent ultrasound limitations. Nemours and Essex independently explain disclosure despite embarrassment; CUH chaperoning plus GMC8,16–22 corroborate explanation/trained observer without a worldwide legal guarantee or permission to delay emergency care.

The three bilingual wording changes explicitly retain atypical-age possibility, assessment during surgery and later atrophy of a preserved testicle. All56 current bilingual paragraphs were read; actions and numerical/population conditions agree.

Washing, activity and follow-up schedules remain local-team instructions. GSTT lower atrophy figure and EAU follow-up cohort estimates are not generalized or pooled; qualitative later atrophy and variable fertility remain. No salvage percentage or hour cutoff is used to postpone assessment.

Medication paragraph4 now distinguishes suspected bacterial infection from nonbacterial management. EAU8.3.1 and RCH epididymo-orchitis pathways support clinical selection, not universal antibiotics or waiting for a culture in a seriously ill infant. Neither treatment replaces urgent torsion assessment.
Medication paragraph3 now gives FDA/RCH independently supported overdose and duplicate-acetaminophen liver risk; no dose, mixing schedule or calculation was added.

bounded_inferences.red_flags-4: Accepted patient-facing implication, explicitly recorded as reasoning from NSW skilled-operator and EAU emergency-clinician manual detorsion, not two verbatim leaflets. Home manipulation could bypass the urgent professional pathway; no home maneuver is taught.
bounded_inferences.medications-3: Accepted patient-specific instruction synthesis: FDA forbids guessing a child amount and RCH directs the child-specific weight/product check. Copying another person’s dose conflicts with those instructions. Actual dose and liver-risk clauses have direct FDA/RCH support; no prescribed amount is inferred.
bounded_inferences.diet-4: Bounded explanation of the materials read: APSA explicitly says children need no special diet; RCH/GSTT support ordinary tolerated intake. Supplements replacing necessary follow-up are not offered as treatment. This is an evidence boundary, not a claim that a comparative diet trial proved every supplement ineffective.
bounded_inferences.prevention-4: Accepted mechanical-protection transfer for the same anatomical situation of one remaining testis. CUH torsion and COG surgical-loss material independently recommend protective clothing/cup; cancer treatment risks, fertility estimates and screening do not transfer. Neither source establishes prevention of spontaneous structural torsion.
